name: Turla – APT Threat Map
description: Técnicas de Turla com cobertura do catálogo (score 3=regra, 2=parcial, 1=lacuna)

techniques.comment: Turla RPC backdoors can upload files from victim machines. | cobertura: regra
Turla surveys a system upon check-in to discover running services and associated processes using the `tasklist /svc` command. | cobertura: regra

Turla surveys a system upon check-in to discover information in the Windows Registry with the `reg query` command. Turla has also retrieved PowerShell payloads hidden in Registry keys as well as checking keys associated with null session named pipes . | cobertura: regra

Turla surveys a system upon check-in to discover network configuration details using the `arp -a`, `nbtstat -n`, `net config`, `ipconfig /all`, and `route` commands, as well as NBTscan. Turla RPC backdoors have also retrieved registered RPC interface information from process memory. | cobertura: regra
Turla has used `tracert` to check internet connectivity. | cobertura: regra

Turla surveys a system upon check-in to discover remote systems on a local network using the `net view` and `net view /DOMAIN` commands. Turla has also used `net group "Domain Computers" /domain`, `net group "Domain Controllers" /domain`, and `net group "Exchange Servers" /domain` to enumerate domain computers, including the organization's DC and Exchange… | cobertura: regra
Turla used `net use` commands to connect to lateral systems within a network. | cobertura: regra
Turla RPC backdoors can collect files from USB thumb drives. | cobertura: lacuna
Based on comparison of Gazer versions, Turla made an effort to obfuscate strings in the malware that could be used as IoCs, including the mutex name and named pipe. | cobertura: regra

Turla has used encryption (including salted 3DES via PowerSploit's `Out-EncryptedScript.ps1`), random variable names, and base64 encoding to obfuscate PowerShell commands and payloads. | cobertura: regra
Turla has used the Registry to store encrypted and encoded payloads. | cobertura: regra
Turla has named components of LunarWeb to mimic Zabbix agent logs. | cobertura: regra

Turla surveys a system upon check-in to discover active local network connections using the `netstat -an`, `net use`, `net file`, and `net session` commands. Turla RPC backdoors have also enumerated the IPv4 TCP connection table via the `GetTcpTable2` API call. | cobertura: regra
Turla has also used PowerSploit's `Invoke-ReflectivePEInjection.ps1` to reflectively load a PowerShell payload into a random process on the victim system. | cobertura: regra
Turla has used Metasploit to perform reflective DLL injection in order to escalate privileges. | cobertura: regra

Turla surveys a system upon check-in to discover running processes using the `tasklist /v` command. Turla RPC backdoors have also enumerated processes associated with specific open ports or named pipes. | cobertura: regra

Turla has used PowerShell to execute commands/scripts, in some cases via a custom executable or code from Empire's PSInject. Turla has also used PowerShell scripts to load and execute malware in memory. | cobertura: regra
Turla RPC backdoors have used cmd.exe to execute commands. | cobertura: regra
Turla has used VBS scripts throughout its operations. | cobertura: regra
Turla has used IronPython scripts as part of the IronNetInjector toolchain to drop payloads. | cobertura: regra
Turla has used various JavaScript-based backdoors. | cobertura: regra
Turla has exploited vulnerabilities in the VBoxDrv.sys driver to obtain kernel mode privileges. | cobertura: regra
Turla has used `net localgroup` and `net localgroup Administrators` to enumerate group information, including members of the local administrators group. | cobertura: regra
Turla has used `net group "Domain Admins" /domain` to identify domain administrators. | cobertura: regra
Turla has used HTTP and HTTPS for C2 communications. | cobertura: regra
Turla has used multiple backdoors which communicate with a C2 server via email attachments. | cobertura: regra
Turla has abused local accounts that have the same password across the victim’s network. | cobertura: regra
Turla surveys a system upon check-in to discover operating system configuration details using the `systeminfo` and `set` commands. | cobertura: regra

Turla surveys a system upon check-in to discover files in specific locations on the hard disk %TEMP% directory, the current user's desktop, the Program Files directory, and Recent. Turla RPC backdoors have also searched for files matching the `lPH*.dll` pattern. | cobertura: regra
Turla has used `net user` to enumerate local accounts on the system. | cobertura: regra
Turla has used `net user /domain` to enumerate domain accounts. | cobertura: regra
Turla RPC backdoors have included local UPnP RPC proxies. | cobertura: regra
Turla has compromised internal network systems to act as a proxy to forward traffic to C2. | cobertura: regra
Turla has used legitimate web services including Pastebin, Dropbox, and GitHub for C2 communications. | cobertura: regra
A Turla JavaScript backdoor has used Google Apps Script as its C2 server. | cobertura: regra
Turla has used shellcode to download Meterpreter after compromising a victim. | cobertura: regra
Turla and its RPC backdoors have used APIs calls for various tasks related to subverting AMSI and accessing then executing commands through RPC and/or named pipes. | cobertura: regra
Turla may attempt to connect to systems within a victim's network using `net use` commands and a predefined list or collection of passwords. | cobertura: regra
Turla has modified Registry values to store payloads. | cobertura: regra
Turla has used `fsutil fsinfo drives` to list connected drives. | cobertura: regra
Turla surveys a system upon check-in to discover the system time by using the `net time` command. | cobertura: regra
Turla RPC backdoors can impersonate or steal process tokens before executing commands. | cobertura: regra

Turla has used a custom decryption routine, which pulls key and salt values from other artifacts such as a WMI filter or PowerShell Profile, to decode encrypted PowerShell payloads. | cobertura: regra
Turla has infected victims using watering holes. | cobertura: regra
Turla has used `net accounts` and `net accounts /domain` to acquire password policy information. | cobertura: regra
Turla has used spearphishing via a link to get users to download and run their malware. | cobertura: regra
Turla has used a custom .NET tool to collect documents from an organization's internal central database. | cobertura: regra
Turla has obtained information on security software, including security logging information that may indicate whether their malware has been detected. | cobertura: regra
Turla has used WMI event filters and consumers to establish persistence. | cobertura: regra
Turla has used PowerShell profiles to maintain persistence on an infected machine. | cobertura: regra

A Turla Javascript backdoor added a local_update_check value under the Registry key `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run` to establish persistence. Additionally, a Turla custom executable containing Metasploit shellcode is saved to the Startup folder to gain persistence. | cobertura: regra
Turla established persistence by adding a Shell value under the Registry key `HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Winlogon`. | cobertura: regra
Turla has modified variables in kernel memory to turn off Driver Signature Enforcement after exploiting vulnerabilities that obtained kernel mode privileges. | cobertura: regra
Turla has gathered credentials from the Windows Credential Manager tool. | cobertura: regra
Turla has encrypted files stolen from connected USB drives into a RAR file before exfiltration. | cobertura: regra
Turla has placed LunarWeb install files into directories that are excluded from scanning. | cobertura: regra
Turla attempted to trick targets into clicking on a link featuring a seemingly legitimate domain from Adobe.com to download their malware and gain initial access. | cobertura: regra
Turla has used WebDAV to upload stolen USB files to a cloud drive. Turla has also exfiltrated stolen files to OneDrive and 4shared. | cobertura: regra
Turla RPC backdoors can be used to transfer files to/from victim machines on the local network. | cobertura: regra
Turla has created web accounts including Dropbox and GitHub for C2 and document exfiltration. | cobertura: lacuna
Turla has used the VPS infrastructure of compromised Iranian threat actors. | cobertura: regra
Turla has used compromised servers as infrastructure. | cobertura: regra
Turla has frequently used compromised WordPress sites for C2 infrastructure. | cobertura: regra
Turla has developed its own unique malware for use in operations. | cobertura: regra
Turla has used malware obtained after compromising other threat actors, such as OilRig. | cobertura: regra
Turla has obtained and customized publicly-available tools like Mimikatz. | cobertura: regra
Turla surveys a system upon check-in to discover Group Policy details using the `gpresult` command. | cobertura: regra
Turla has used a AMSI bypass, which patches the in-memory amsi.dll, in PowerShell scripts to bypass Windows antimalware products. | cobertura: regra
